chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Salih ibn Sa'id, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'From chivalry is the improvement of wealth.'

key_terms.الْمُرُوءَة: Chivalry, manliness, or noble character traits

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet say about the relationship between chivalry and wealth management?
ai.summary: In the context of al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq links material stewardship to spiritual chivalry, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing worldly duties with religious obligations. This narration underscores that acquiring and managing wealth responsibly is not merely economic but a moral imperative (murū'ah) that enables one to fulfill social and religious responsibilities effectively.
